HD.rationale: Home Depot is a high-quality franchise with dominant market position, scale advantages, and a growing Pro ecosystem, but the fundamental trajectory is mixed. Q1 FY2026 showed +4.8% YoY revenue growth and comps turning positive for the first time in 2 years, yet EPS declined -4.3% YoY and -8.8% QoQ, reflecting margin compression from acquisition integration (SRS, GMS, Mingledorff's) and a softer housing backdrop. Operating margin fell to ~11.9% and ROIC compressed from 31.3% to 25.4%. The balance sheet carries meaningful leverage (total liabilities $94B vs equity $13.9B). On valuation, the current P/E of 24.1x sits near the middle of its 12-month range (20.3-28.8x) and slightly above the forward P/E of 21.1x, which is below its 5-year median of 22.27x — suggesting fair-to-slightly-cheap pricing vs own history. The stock has been range-bound (down ~21% from 52-week high of $426.75). Near-term catalysts are limited: Q2 earnings on Aug 18 could provide a read-through on Pro demand and margin stabilization, and the 21st Century ROAD to Housing Act provides a modest structural tailwind, but housing lock-in effects and elevated rates (10Y at 4.54%) remain headwinds. News sentiment is moderately positive (mean 0.44). Overall, a solid franchise at a fair price with earnings trajectory still under pressure — mildly attractive but not compelling.
